name: CoinsPaid
rootCause: Recently, Estonian encrypted payment service provider CoinsPaid said it suffered a cyber attack and $37.3 million worth of cryptocurrency was stolen. Although the attack caused significant financial losses to the company and had many adverse effects on the usability of the payment platform, the company stated that customer funds are still safe and the incident will not have a significant impact on the company's business. CoinsPaid said the attack was initiated by the Lazarus hacking group, and their goal was to obtain higher cash. On July 26, SlowMist tweeted that CoinsPaid, Atomic and Alphapo attackers may all be the North Korean hacker organization Lazarus Group.

descriptions.text: Recently, Estonian encrypted payment service provider CoinsPaid said it suffered a cyber attack and $37.3 million worth of cryptocurrency was stolen. Although the attack caused significant financial losses to the company and had many adverse effects on the usability of the payment platform, the company stated that customer funds are still safe and the incident will not have a significant impact on the company's business. CoinsPaid said the attack was initiated by the Lazarus hacking group, and their goal was to obtain higher cash. On July 26, SlowMist tweeted that CoinsPaid, Atomic and Alphapo attackers may all be the North Korean hacker organization Lazarus Group.

On 22 July 2023, CoinsPaid was compromised through a sophisticated social engineering attack attributed to the Lazarus Group, resulting in the theft of $37.3 million. Attackers gained access by manipulating an employee and exploiting a cluster-level vulnerability. An attacker posing as a recruiter convinced a CoinsPaid employee to install malware, enabling access to internal infrastructure. Attackers exploited a vulnerable application to open a backdoor and issue legitimate withdrawal requests, bypassing traditional controls.
